frames.title: RunLog
frames.explanation: **One run, as the user can read it.** RunLog turns a run's event stream into timestamped lines — every read, every long think, every set_plan reply and its issues — and watches for a model stuck re-reading files it has already read. The run's reader feeds onEvent; the run's own code calls note, retry and end; listeners (the status bar, the run log window) are notified on the calling thread.

steps.ttsText: RunLog keeps one line per thing the model did during a run: every file read, every long think, every set_plan reply and its issues. The status bar only shows the latest line, so this log is what lets the run log window replay the whole story.
Everything arrives here, in onEvent, a when over the run's event stream. Thinking is timed from ThinkingStart until the next tool or text arrives, and a new host gets a line of its own.

A tool call is where the loop warning fires: the call is logged through toolLine, which counts re-reads, and the moment rereads crosses REREAD_WARN the log records that the model may have lost the task.

toolLine turns a Read into a line range and checks it against every range already read from that file: an overlap counts as a re-read, and the fourth one sets the looping warning. Anything else is logged as a plain Read, with the span when one was asked for.

frames.title: RunLog
frames.explanation: **One run, as the user can read it.** RunLog turns a run's event stream into timestamped lines — every read, every long think, every set_plan reply and its issues — and watches for a model stuck re-reading files it has already read. The run's reader feeds onEvent; the run's own code calls note, retry and end; listeners (the status bar, the run log window) are notified on the calling thread.

steps.ttsText: RunLog keeps one line per thing the model did during a run: every file read, every long think, every set_plan reply and its issues. The status bar only shows the latest line, so this log is what lets the run log window replay the whole story.
Everything arrives here, in onEvent, a when over the run's event stream. Thinking is timed from ThinkingStart until the next tool or text arrives, and a new host gets a line of its own.

A tool call is where the loop warning fires: the call is logged through toolLine, which counts re-reads, and the moment rereads crosses REREAD_WARN the log records that the model may have lost the task.

toolLine turns a Read into a line range and checks it against every range already read from that file: an overlap counts as a re-read, and the fourth one sets the looping warning. Anything else is logged as a plain Read, with the span when one was asked for.
